A '''stormtrooper''' of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was part of an Imperial entourage that searched homes on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] during the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] holiday of [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]] in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]]. Searching for ties to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], the Empire [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|blockaded]] the world and declared martial law. The [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] was one of two Imperial [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] who accompanied a [[Unidentified Imperial commander (Blockade of Kashyyyk)|commander]] and a [[Unidentified Imperial technician|technician]], with the other trooper designated [[B4711]].

The cadre entered the [[Chewbacca's home|home]] of the famous Rebel [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], who was not home, but they remained inside to terrorize [[Chewbacca's family/Legends|Chewbacca's family]] and his [[Human/Legends|human]] friend [[Saun Dann]]. At one point, the residence's [[wallscreen]] aired a program began that announced itself as required viewing for all members of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial forces]]. Entitled ''[[Life on Tatooine]]'', it was a live broadcast of a harrowing night in the life of [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], the nightshift [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] of a [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|cantina]] in the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine's]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].

All four Imperials viewed the program, and the distraction allowed Chewbacca's son [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpy]] to transmit a "return to base" order to the commander's [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] from his [[mini-transmitter]]. The stormtrooper departed with the two [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers]], but B4711 was left behind to await Chewbacca's return.

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Factor in the song by Jefferson Starship, the holographic circus troupe, some ineffectual Imperial antagonists (including the Wilhelm-screaming stormtrooper, B4711), and it's no wonder the ''Star Wars'' Holiday Special is accused of having an identity crisis.|Alex Newborn|<ref name="Bad Feeling">{{InsiderCite|106|I Have a Bad Feeling About This!}}</ref>}}
Unlike B4711, this stormtrooper is not named in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''. The ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} script establishes that this trooper is less menacing than B4711, being referred to as the "less-menacing trooper" until accepting an offered [[Wookiee-ookiee]] from Saun Dann. The script then refers to the trooper as the "cookiee trooper." Ultimately, however, the scene with the trooper accepting the cookie was cut from the script's fourth draft.<ref name="script">{{WebCite|url=http://starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/script.htm|text=The Fourth Draft Script &ndash; 09/13/78|work=[[Starwarsholidayspecial.com|The Star Wars Holiday Special]]|archivedate=20101223071504}}</ref>

In the [[Star Wars Insider 106|106th issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'', author [[Alex Newborn]] called the trooper and his comrades "ineffectual Imperial antagonists."<ref name="Bad Feeling" />
